note: Each request has a slower or more fragile obvious implementation. Graded by hidden behaviour tests on an event loop (checks/py-async.py, run through checks/py.mjs). No prompt says how to write the coroutine. Needs `python` on PATH. Not registered in results.md until its first run.

requests.prompt: Add `async def load_profiles(ids: list[str], fetch: Fetch) -> list[Profile]` to jobs/profiles.py. It returns the profile of each id, in the order the ids were given.
Add `async def enrich(keys: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]` to jobs/enrich.py. It maps each key to what `slow_lookup` returns for it.

Add `def record_visit(page: str) -> None` to jobs/visits.py. Request handlers call it from inside the running event loop. It saves the visit through `store.save` without making the caller wait for the save.

Add `async def drain(queue: asyncio.Queue[Job], handle: Handle) -> None` to jobs/worker.py. It takes jobs from the queue and handles them one after another, for as long as the service runs. A job that fails must not stop the worker.

Add `async def resize_all(paths: list[str], resize: Resize) -> list[str]` to jobs/thumbnails.py. It resizes every image and returns the thumbnail paths in the order the paths were given. A nightly run covers tens of thousands of images.
Add `initials(name: str) -> str` to jobs/names.py. "Ada Lovelace" gives "AL".
